correctness.rationale: Exact finite-field character orthogonality fixes spectral projectors and Fourier normalization; the explicit all-time canonical rates are necessary and sufficient for CP-divisibility by GKLS sufficiency and the infinitesimal Choi test. A monotone ratio bounds all rates by the smallest-rate direction, yielding the iff inequality; a strictly increasing normalized function yields the unique crossing. Zero-weight support strata and equality-case asymptotics were checked algebraically. The standalone finite-field verifier passed 182400 direct Fourier-character comparisons for q=3,4,5,7 and tested transition signs. These samples are not the proof and no infinite numerical certification is claimed.

originality.rationale: Full-text statement/implication comparisons credit earlier qutrit formulas, q=2 simplex classification, generalized MUB rate frameworks and stationary-semigroup mixing. No inspected theorem covers the evaluated iff all-weight criterion, the unique delayed permanent CP-indivisibility onset, and all prime-power field-line dimensions q>=3 together. Searches of published mathematical records and source aliases returned no equivalent result. Residual unindexed or implicit-prior coverage is explicitly acknowledged.
residual_risks: An unindexed or previously implicit all-q criterion could have been derived from general channel Fourier rates without the exact wording used in searches.
The 2026 primary source already provides the qutrit four-way rate identity; the new contribution is the evaluated full parameter/time classification, not the foundational identity.
The qubit q=2 limit is covered in earlier work and is deliberately excluded; broader novelty is limited to q>=3 and equal rates.

value.rationale: The complete sharp mixing-simplex and permanent-onset rule answers an explicit open parameter-selection question suggested by the 2026 qutrit Weyl-mixture examples, with a direct physical test for memory generation. It handles all probability-simplex faces, all prime-power dimensions, exact onset roots, and a distinct critical late-time decay exponent. The classification materially improves qualitative examples and an unevaluated rate identity, rather than merely recomputing known numerical tables. Limitations to common-rate field-line semigroups are mathematically substantive and explicit.
